problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+8y=5{e}^{2x}+3{e}^{3x}
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-2x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

We see that the right-hand side is $5{e}^{2x}+3{e}^{3x},$ and neither ${e}^{2x}$ nor ${e}^{3x}$ is a term in the complementary solution, so we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha {e}^{2x}+\beta {e}^{3x},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=2\alpha {e}^{2x}+3\beta {e}^{3x}.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2\alpha {e}^{2x}+3\beta {e}^{3x})+8(\alpha {e}^{2x}+\beta {e}^{3x}) & =5{e}^{2x}+3{e}^{3x} \\ (8\alpha +8\alpha ){e}^{2x}+(12\beta +8\beta ){e}^{3x} & =5{e}^{2x}+3{e}^{3x} \\ 16\alpha {e}^{2x}+20\beta {e}^{3x} & =5{e}^{2x}+3{e}^{3x}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients of ${e}^{2x}$ and ${e}^{3x},$ respectively, gives

$$
16\alpha =5,\,\,20\beta =3.
$$

So, we have

$$
\alpha =\frac{5}{16},\,\,\beta =\frac{3}{20}.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\frac{5}{16}{e}^{2x}+\frac{3}{20}{e}^{3x}.
$$
